name: Starter: Persian
about: Standard written Persian word order, ezafe, and compound verbs in useful everyday situations, with needed vowel marks shown until you know each word.

words.بودن: to be (اَست: is; هَستَم: I am; نیست: isn't; بود: was)
words.شما: you, polite or to more than one
words.داشتن: to have (دارَم: I have; نَدارَم: I don't have)
words.زدن: to hit (in two-word verbs: زَنگ زَدَن: to call)
words.کردن: to do, make (in two-word verbs: کار کَردَن: to work)
words.رفتن: to go (می‌رَوَم: I go; بِرَوَم: that I go)
words.حال: state, how you are (حالَت چِطُور اَست: how are you)
words.ما: we, us (مُنتَظِرِ ماست: is waiting for us)
words.برگشتن: to come back (بَرمی‌گَردی: you come back)
words.خوردن: to eat or drink (خُوردیم: we ate; می‌خُوری: you drink)
words.سر: head (سَرِ کار: at or to work)
words.گرفتن: to take, get (یاد گِرِفتَن: to learn)
words.باریدن: to rain (می‌بارَد: it rains, it will rain)

zendegi-kardan.about: Literally to do life: زِندِگی می‌کُنَم, I live.

kar-kardan.about: Literally to do work; چِه کار می‌کُنی؟ means “what are you doing?”

dorost-kardan.about: Literally to make right: شام دُرُست کَردَن, to make dinner.

chay-khordan.about: خُوردَن (to eat) is also used for drinking: چای می‌خُوری؟

sar-e-kar.about: Literally at the head of work: سَرِ کار می‌رَوَم, I go to work.

akhar-e-hafte.about: Literally the end of the week.

zang-zadan.about: Literally to hit the bell: بِه تُو زَنگ می‌زَنَم, I'll call you.

khabar-dadan.about: Literally to give news: بِه مَن خَبَر بِدِه, let me know.

concept.line: A Persian sentence usually ends with its verb, with the object before it: مَن قَهوه می‌نوشَم (I drink coffee); فَردا بِه سَرِ کار می‌رَوَم.
Most present-tense verbs are می, the present stem and an ending for who: می‌رَوَم, می‌رَوی, می‌رَوَد, می‌رَویم; context lets the same form mean go, am going, or, with a future time word, will go.

words.means: هستید = you are; نیستم = I am not

concept.line: اَست means is; short forms for am and are can attach to the preceding word (خَسته‌اَم: I am tired; خوابَند: they are asleep), while full forms also occur (دانِشجو هَستَم).

words.means: دارم = I have; دارید = you have; ندارم = I do not have

concept.line: Persian has no word for the; a bare noun can be definite from context (کِتاب رویِ میز اَست), یِک means one or a, and the suffix ـی means a or some: یِک کِتاب, کِتابی.

words.means: می‌زنید = you speak; می‌زنم = I speak
نمی‌فهمم = I do not understand; می‌فهمید = you understand

concept.line: A yes/no question keeps a statement's order and only the voice rises (اِنگِلیسی صُحبَت می‌کُنی؟), and formal آیا may begin it; a question word stays where the answer would be: کُجا زِندِگی می‌کُنی؟

words.means: می‌کنم = I do; می‌کنید = you do; می‌کند = does
می‌روم = I go; می‌روید = you go; می‌رود = goes

concept.line: The ezafe is an e or ye that links a noun, adjective, or word such as روی or بِدون to what follows; it is usually unwritten, but the app's readings show it as ِ or ـهٔ: اِسمِ مَن, خانهٔ بُزُرگ, رویِ میز, بِدونِ شِکَر, مُنتَظِرِ ما.
